included.label: Included points
included.copy: Recorded points with enough clear information about the full point to use in these charts.

break.label: Break points
break.copy: Points in a regular game where the receiver would win the game by winning this point, whether the chance is taken or saved. Tiebreak points do not count.

serve.label: Serve
serve.copy: A serve attempt, including faults, lets, aces and double faults. A fault or let need not end the point.

return.label: Return
return.copy: The receiver’s attempt to hit the serve back, including errors.

plus1.label: Serve +1
plus1.copy: The server’s first attempt to hit the ball after the return, including errors.

rally.label: Later Rally
rally.copy: Play after the server’s first attempted shot following the return.

reach.label: Stage reached
reach.copy: The point got as far as a shot attempt at this stage; one point can reach several stages.

conditional.label: Win rate after reaching a stage
conditional.copy: The player’s wins out of the points known to reach this stage, shown separately when serving and receiving.

ending.label: Ending types
ending.copy: Descriptions in the match record of the final shot, error or point award.

recorded.label: Recorded points
recorded.copy: All points in the match records for this player and view, including omitted points and points from excluded match records.

retention.label: Included percentage
retention.copy: The included points as a percentage of all recorded points for this player and view, not their whole career.

omitted.label: Points omitted because details are unclear
omitted.copy: Recorded points left out of the charts because their details are unclear or conflicting.

excluded.label: Points from excluded match records
excluded.copy: Recorded points left out because the match may have ended early or its ending cannot be confirmed from the record.

matches.label: All recorded matches
matches.copy: The player’s points pooled across the matches recorded here, rather than their whole career.

dates.label: Dates in the match records
dates.copy: The dates listed for these matches, without proof of when their details became available.

categories.label: Men’s and women’s categories
categories.copy: The categories used in the match records, without confirming which tennis tour each match belongs to.

basis.label: Points counted for a percentage
basis.copy: The total number of points a percentage is measured out of.

endshare.label: Ending win and loss percentages
endshare.copy: The selected player’s wins or losses ending at a stage, out of all included points in the chosen selection.

typeshare.label: Ending-type percentages
typeshare.copy: Points with a given recorded ending, out of the included points ending at that same stage in the chosen selection.

faced.label: Break points faced
faced.copy: Included break points on the selected player’s serve, when the opponent could win the game by winning the point.

opportunities.label: Break-point opportunities
opportunities.copy: Included break points when the selected player is receiving and could win the game by winning the point.

notreached.label: Did not reach this stage
notreached.copy: The point is known to have ended before this stage.

unknown.label: Stage reach unclear
unknown.copy: The record does not clearly show whether the point reached this stage.

zero.label: Zero
zero.copy: No events of that kind were recorded among the points counted.

unavailable.label: Unavailable
unavailable.copy: No percentage can be shown because no points qualify for it or the needed information is unclear.

ace.label: Ace
ace.copy: A serve recorded as winning the point without the receiver touching the ball.

doublefault.label: Double fault
doublefault.copy: A second-serve fault that loses the point.

winner.label: Other recorded winner
winner.copy: A shot other than an ace that the match record marks as a winner.

forced.label: Forced error
forced.copy: An error the match record describes as a forced response to the opponent’s shot.

unforced.label: Unforced error
unforced.copy: An error the match record describes as a miss not forced by the opponent’s shot.

administrative.label: No recorded final shot
administrative.copy: An ending with no final shot named in the record, such as a point penalty or failed challenge.

otherending.label: Other recorded ending
otherending.copy: An ending marked unreturnable, without a recorded forced- or unforced-error label.

unknownending.label: Unknown ending type
unknownending.copy: The record does not clearly show how the point ended.

finalplayer.label: Player making the final action
finalplayer.copy: The player who made the last recorded shot or error, who may differ from the player who won the point.

sides.label: Selected player and opponent
sides.copy: The selected player is the player you chose above; the opponent is the other player in that match.

noactor.label: No final-shot player named
noactor.copy: This ending gives a point result without naming a player’s final shot.

unknownactor.label: Final-action player unclear
unknownactor.copy: The record does not clearly identify who made the final action.

intro: “When” means the stage of a point. Explore <button type="button" class="definition-trigger" id="term-included" aria-describedby="definition-text-included" data-definition="included" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="definition-panel">included points</button> from recorded matches, 2021–2025. The ending identifies the final recorded action, not the shot that caused the result.
guide: Illustrative example, not a player result: with 100 included points, 10 wins and 5 losses ending at <button type="button" class="definition-trigger" id="term-guide-serve" data-definition="serve" aria-describedby="definition-text-serve" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="definition-panel">Serve</button> would occupy 10% and 5% of the ending chart. Both use all 100 points. A win rate after a stage uses only the points that reached it; reaching several stages counts the same shared point more than once.
limitations:
• Missing point details may change the apparent pattern of endings. Missing details occur especially later in rallies.
  • These are sampled charted matches, with unequal opponent exposure. Included percentages do not measure a player’s career or complete tournament coverage.
  • Consistent match records do not prove the match officially finished. The men’s/women’s labels do not confirm which tennis tour each match belongs to.
  • Recorded endings do not establish what caused a point result, player rankings, strengths or clutch ability. Break points describe a selected subset.
  • Uncertainty intervals have not been established. All acquired years are exposed, and chart date labels do not verify historical availability.
methodology:
Profiles describe included chart-observed points, not all points played. Missing or unsupported later-rally notation accounts for much of the omission and may affect phase proportions. Points from excluded match records and points omitted after notation checks are retained in coverage; they are not assigned success, failure or known absence.

Break-point context is reconciled pre-point ordinary-game score: every opportunity counts, tiebreaks never count, and unknown/conflicting states stay outside the subset. This annotation never rescues withheld points. The subset selector changes the denominator to included break points; serving/receiving counts distinguish facing a break from having a break opportunity. Point endings partition the selected included subset. Win share = recorded wins at that ending / the selected included subset involving the selected player; loss share uses recorded losses over that same denominator. The phase names the final recorded action by either player, not its causal contribution. First-serve faults and lets do not automatically end points.

Stage reach = points known to reach the stage / selected included subset points. Stages overlap and describe a shared point, not both players executing the stroke. Role-specific point win rate = selected-player wins among points reaching the stage / the documented role-specific reached-point denominator. Unknown reaches stay outside that denominator; an unknown winner among reached points makes the rate unavailable. Unknown is not absence or a loss; zero-denominator rates remain unavailable.

Ending types reflect recorded notation and the linked terminal actor, not causal credit. Aces and double faults are separate; collapsed unreturnable notation is Other supported ending, without inferred forced-error attribution. Administrative endings are nonphysical. Type percentages use the displayed phase denominator; absent observations are not errors.

Serve +1 is the server’s first attempt to hit the ball after the return, including errors. It remains owned exclusively by Rally; its breakdown adds no extra factor credit. Return belongs to Return, and Serve to Serve.

Unequal exposure and selective retention prevent fair player comparisons, rankings, causal-skill, transferable-skill or independent-factor conclusions. There are no established confidence intervals. Internal chart consistency does not establish official match completion or complete tournament coverage. Historical men’s/women’s labels do not certify governing-tour membership. Names are exact source identities, without alias merging. All acquired years are exposed; source-date labels do not establish historical availability.

Only the exact men’s-category Dominik Koepfer identity is hidden from selection. All 450 identities, his unavailable profiles and all coverage totals remain embedded. No historical data is removed or recalculated; the separately frozen context extension supplies subset and ending-type displays.

Typography: Fraunces is embedded from the portfolio’s saved, licensed local asset. Source Serif 4 and IBM Plex Mono are requested by name, with Georgia and system-monospace fallbacks; cached binaries are not embedded because their saved rights were not verified.
